_note: Phố, nước và một phần mốc trích từ OpenStreetMap qua Overpass API, đã đơn giản hoá (Douglas–Peucker 4–6 m) để chạy offline: không tile, không thư viện, không gọi mạng lúc dùng. Mốc du lịch chính, lộ trình và lớp tranh là nội dung tuyển chọn tay. THỨ TỰ MỐC LÀ HỢP ĐỒNG: route.js trỏ theo `sight:<chỉ số>`, nên mốc tuyển chọn phải giữ nguyên vị trí 0..N-1, mốc OSM nối thêm vào sau, và mốc bổ sung cho vùng cũ chỉ được nối vào CUỐI mảng. Đây là bản đồ ĐỊNH HƯỚNG, không thay bản đồ dẫn đường.

landmarks.note: The 18th-century covered bridge on the 20,000₫ note. Ticketed to cross.
Two-storey merchant house beside the bridge. Trapdoor in the floor for flood season.
Cantonese congregation hall. Red-and-gold courtyard, dragon fountain.
Working silk and lantern workshop. Short traditional music sets through the day.

landmarks.n: Bảo tàng Văn hoá Sa Huỳnh
landmarks.note: Burial jars and bronze from the Sa Huynh culture, 2,000 years before the port.
Seven generations of one family. Japanese, Chinese and Vietnamese joinery in one room.
The largest assembly hall. Dedicated to Thiên Hậu, protector of sailors.
Cham-era well down a narrow alley. Cao lầu is said to need this water.
Private ancestral chapel in a walled garden. Still used by the family.
Temple to general Quan Công, facing the market. Traders came here to swear oaths.
Produce in the morning, cooked food all day. The cheapest prices in the old town.
Where the paper-lantern boats launch after dark. Agree the fare before boarding.
Crossing to Cẩm Nam island. Chè bắp and bánh đập are the reason to walk over.
Western crossing out of the old town, named for a local revolutionary.
An old house open without a ticket. There is usually a shop inside.

landmarks.n: Bảo tàng Gốm sứ Mậu dịch
landmarks.note: Ceramics raised from the harbour and from wrecks — the port's reach, in shards.
The town's main history museum, from the Sa Huỳnh era to the trading port.
Neighbourhood pagoda west of the old town. Quiet, few visitors.
Where residents actually shop. Outside the ticketed zone, so prices run lower.
Fabric by the metre and tailors upstairs. Agree the price and the date in writing.
Lantern stalls and street food after dark, on the An Hội side of the river.
A former pharmacy and trading house. The family collection is upstairs.
The produce row of the riverside market — a place to buy fruit, not a sight.
Small neighbourhood temple. Name as recorded in OpenStreetMap; the sign outside may read differently.

landmarks.n: Nhà biểu diễn nghệ thuật cổ truyền
landmarks.note: Short sets of traditional music and dance through the day, on the old-town ticket.
Hainanese congregation hall, raised in memory of merchants lost at sea.
Teochew hall. The carved woodwork is the reason to step inside.
Memorial to the Polish conservator whose survey work helped save the old town.
The lane that lights up after dark. Busiest roughly 18:00–21:00.
A concrete blockhouse left from the colonial period, on the edge of town.
A 300-year-old Chinese merchant house, one room wide and very long. On the old-town ticket.
The footbridge to the lantern island. Where the paper-lantern sellers stand after dark.
The workshops that supply the town's lanterns. Bamboo frames split by hand at the front.
The town's Catholic church, a short walk north of the protected core.
The river island across the bridge. Chè bắp, bánh đập and hến trộn are made here.

art._note: Tranh vẽ tay dùng làm nền, nhìn THẲNG TỪ TRÊN XUỐNG nên tỉ lệ đồng nhất hai chiều. Tấm TRƯỚC phải bỏ vì địa lý bịa: trong đó Chùa Cầu bắc qua sông lớn, mà ngoài đời nó bắc qua một con lạch chừng 18m còn Thu Bồn là dòng khác cách một dãy phố — nên mốc thứ hai rơi xuống giữa lòng sông và ghim quán ven sông theo xuống nước. Tấm này vẽ đúng thế đất: sông chạy ngang phía nam, phố cổ phía bắc, con lạch có cầu mái ở rìa tây, An Hội và Cẩm Nam ở hai góc dưới. Mốc 1 là cây cầu mái đó; mốc 2 suy ra bằng số học từ giả định BẮC Ở TRÊN và tỉ lệ 0,75 px/m — tỉ lệ này đo từ khoảng cách thật 133m giữa Chùa Cầu và bờ bắc sông, ứng với 100px trong tranh. Bố cục từng con phố vẫn là ấn tượng của người vẽ; bản đồ chính xác là bản vector ở Open full map.
art.alt: Illustrated map looking straight down on Hoi An Ancient Town, the Thu Bon river and the covered bridge

routes.name: Lantern Walk Route
routes.blurb: Wander slowly, greet locals, and let Hội An find you.

stops.tip: Visit at sunset for the best lantern reflections on the water.
Ask to see the flood marks on the wall — they go up past head height.
The courtyard is quietest just after it opens.
Agree the boat price before stepping in, and count the lanterns you get.

streets.n: Lối vào Thư viện Quốc gia Phố Tràng Thi
Quảng trường Cách mạng Tháng Tám
Quảng trường Cách mạng Tháng Tám
Lối đi nội bộ Chợ Hàng Da

landmarks.note: The lake the old city grew around; a full loop walks in half an hour. The roads circling it close to traffic on weekend evenings.
A 19th-century temple on an islet in the lake, reached only by the red bridge. Small entrance fee; quietest just after it opens.
The old quarter's big covered market: cloth and household goods by the crate inside, food stalls along the lanes on its flanks.
The short red wooden bridge out to Ngoc Son temple — the most photographed twenty metres in Hanoi, and a crush at sunset.
The 1902 steel bridge over the Red River. Trains still take the middle track; a narrow footpath runs the whole length past market gardens.

landmarks.n: Bảo tàng Công an Hà Nội
Bảo tàng Lịch sử Quốc gia Việt Nam
landmarks.note: Bronze-age drums through to 1945, in a 1930s building that deliberately mixed French structure with Vietnamese roofs.
The French résidence supérieure, taken in the August 1945 uprising. A state guesthouse now, so it is a look-from-the-gate landmark.
A pagoda down a lane beside the cathedral, easy to walk straight past. Inside is a courtyard the street noise does not reach.
An old pagoda wedged into the shophouse row on Hàng Đường, keeping its bell tower between two rows of sweet shops.
Dedicated to the monk-healer of the Ly court, on the small street named after him a block from the cathedral.
Seat of the national Buddhist sangha and a working city pagoda — packed on the first and fifteenth of each lunar month.
The French colonial prison, later the “Hanoi Hilton”. Most of it is a hotel now; one wing is the museum.
The last of the old city's sixteen gates, built in 1749 and still straddling the street.
Friday to Sunday nights the main north–south lane closes to traffic and fills with stalls.
The oldest temple in the old quarter, guarding its eastern gate since the 11th century.
The beer corner. Plastic stools go out on the road from late afternoon; the road is the seating.
The 1911 opera house at the end of Tràng Tiền, modelled on the Palais Garnier.

routes.name: Hoan Kiem Loop
routes.blurb: One slow lap of the lake, ending in the old quarter.

stops.tip: Early morning is when the lake belongs to the neighbourhood.
The red bridge is busiest at midday.
Go for the food lane behind the market, not the market itself.

art._note: Tranh vẽ tay dùng làm nền. Hai mốc neo vào HAI ĐẦU HỒ Hoàn Kiếm — vật duy nhất trong tranh đo được chắc chắn — nên tỉ lệ và hướng là thật, còn vị trí tuyệt đối của từng mái nhà thì không. Riêng đảo Ngọc Sơn được vẽ sát đầu hồ hơn thực tế chừng 60m, nên ghim Đền Ngọc Sơn rơi hơi lệch xuống nam so với hòn đảo trong tranh.
art.alt: Illustrated aerial map of Hoan Kiem lake and the Hanoi Old Quarter

landmarks.note: The market under the clock tower. Souvenir aisles at the front quote tourist prices; the food counters are along the sides.
Built 1877–1880 from brick shipped out of Marseille. A long restoration keeps the inside shut on and off — the facade is the sight.
The 1891 post office next to the cathedral, still selling stamps under the original iron arches and painted wall maps.

landmarks.n: Bia Kỷ Niệm Lễ Độc Lập
Bia Kỷ Niệm Sự Kiện Đấu Tranh Ngày 19/3/1950
Bia Tưởng Niệm Trận Đánh Tòa Đại Sứ Mỹ
Bảo tàng Chứng tích Chiến tranh
landmarks.note: Photographs, ordnance and aircraft from the American war, told from the Vietnamese side. Heavy going; leave time afterwards.

landmarks.n: Bảo tàng Mỹ thuật Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh
landmarks.note: Vietnamese painting and lacquer inside a 1930s merchant mansion — the tiled floors and stained glass are half of what you came for.

landmarks.n: Bảo tàng Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh
landmarks.note: City history in the former Gia Long Palace, with the 1962 bunker and its escape tunnel under the front lawn.

landmarks.n: Di Tích Chuồng Chim Bồ Câu Người Ấn Tamil

landmarks.note: Rebuilt in 1966 and kept as it stood on the April 1975 morning a tank came through the gate — war room and bunker included.

landmarks.n: Giáo xứ Chợ Đũi - Nhà thờ Huyện Sĩ
landmarks.note: A 1905 church paid for by the Huyện Sĩ family, whose tomb lies behind the altar. Rarely more than a handful of visitors.
A roundabout with a concrete pavilion over a pond. After dark the pavement around it becomes one of the district's snack streets.

landmarks.n: Miếu Năm Bà Ngũ Hành Tao Đàn

landmarks.note: The pedestrian boulevard from City Hall to the river. Busiest after 20:00.
A shaded lane of bookshops and coffee beside the cathedral.
The long park beside the market, and the terminus for most city buses.
The 1897 opera house on Đồng Khởi, between the two colonial hotels.

routes.name: The Colonial Spine
routes.blurb: Three blocks that hold most of what the French left standing.

stops.tip: Start at the market. Everything here is negotiable and the first price is not the price.
The cathedral has been under restoration for years — the outside is the point.
The post office still works as a post office. Postcards at the back, on the left.

art._note: Tranh vẽ tay dùng làm nền. Hai mốc neo vào Chợ Bến Thành và Nhà thờ Đức Bà, hai công trình vẽ rõ mặt bằng nên chấm được chính xác; tranh nghiêng 6° so với bắc và phép neo đã tính phần nghiêng đó.
art.alt: Illustrated aerial map of District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, along the Saigon river

landmarks.note: Steel dragon over the river. It breathes fire and then water at 21:00 on Saturday and Sunday.
The largest collection of Cham stone carving anywhere, in the 1915 pavilion built to hold it.
Food and dried goods below, fabric and tailoring above. Prices are asked, not fixed.
Where the city actually eats. The ground-floor food court is the cheapest hot meal in the centre.
Pink 1923 French cathedral with a rooster on the spire instead of a cross — hence the local name.
A swing bridge: the centre span turns side-on around 01:00 to let ships through, then turns back.

landmarks.n: Cầu Tình yêu · Cá chép hoá rồng
landmarks.note: A short pier of heart-shaped locks beside a carp turning into a dragon. The night crowd's meeting point.
City-centre pagoda with a garden courtyard, open through the day.
The Nguyễn fort that held off the first French attack in 1858. Vauban plan, low earth walls.
City history in the citadel grounds, including the 1858 siege and the American build-out of the port.
A single leaning mast holding the whole deck on cables. Lit in changing colour after dark.
Where the night river boats leave. Agree the price and the route before boarding, not after.

landmarks.n: Bảo tàng Mỹ Thuật Đà nẵng
landmarks.note: Three floors of central-Vietnamese painting, folk craft and Cham-influenced work. Small, air-conditioned, almost never crowded.
A small riverside pagoda beside the Cham museum, older than nearly everything standing around it.
A teaching pagoda on Phan Châu Trinh with a Buddhist school in the back courtyard — busy with young monks at midday.
A neighbourhood market well off the tourist rows — breakfast noodles in the morning and no menus in English.
The east-bank night market by the Dragon Bridge: grilled seafood, skewers and sugarcane juice from six until late.
A riverside park under a wing-shaped canopy, built for the 2017 summit and lit after dark — the local evening walking spot.
The city's main theatre, on the roundabout by the market: touring companies, traditional opera nights and school galas.

landmarks.n: Nhà thờ Chính tòa Đà Nẵng
Nhà thờ Giáo xứ An Hải

landmarks.note: The largest Cao Dai temple in central Vietnam, the all-seeing eye above the altar. Services run four times a day; visitors sit at the back.

routes.name: Han River After Dark
routes.blurb: Market, cathedral, then the two bridges — timed to end at the dragon.

stops.tip: Eat before you walk. The market's food floor closes early evening.
The rooster on the spire is easier to spot from across the road.
The locks and the carp are the meeting point; it gets crowded by 20:30.
Fire and water at 21:00, Saturday and Sunday. Stand upwind of the head.

art._note: Tranh vẽ tay dùng làm nền, nhìn THẲNG TỪ TRÊN XUỐNG (orthographic) nên tỉ lệ đồng nhất theo cả hai chiều — đó là điều kiện để artmap.js neo được bằng phép đồng dạng hai mốc. Lượt sinh đầu xin góc phối cảnh và phải bỏ: hai cầu cách nhau 1113m chỉ chiếm 285px trong khi con sông rộng 700m chiếm 450px, tức hai tỉ lệ lệch nhau năm lần, và mọi ghim bờ tây rơi xuống giữa sông. Hai mốc dưới đây là giữa nhịp cầu Rồng và giữa nhịp cầu sông Hàn: 1113m thật trên 725px tranh, ra 0,651 px/m, và con sông trong tranh rộng ra khoảng 460m — khớp sông Hàn thật. Bố cục phố vẫn là ấn tượng của người vẽ; bản đồ chính xác là bản vector ở Open full map.
art.alt: Illustrated map looking straight down on the Han river in Da Nang, the Dragon Bridge and the riverside streets

streets.n: Đường Khách sạn Mỹ Khê II
Đường Khách sạn Mỹ Khê II

landmarks.note: Open sand the length of the city. Lifeguards fly flags — red means the rip is running.
Vietnam's first floodlit night-swimming beach, open through the evening in summer.
The public end of the beach: showers, free parking and a lantern-lit square behind it.
The northern beach entrance, with the largest square and the most food carts after sunset.
Two blocks of bars, western food and late-night bún. The backpacker end of the beach.
The neighbourhood market behind the beach. Seafood here costs a fraction of the beach road.
The quiet southern end of the strip, below the hotel line.
The neighbourhood pagoda two blocks back from the sand, a courtyard of quiet between the hotel streets.
The market inland from the beach where the neighbourhood actually shops: breakfast bún, cheap fruit, no English.
Market for the streets behind My Khe. Busiest before eight in the morning, half shut by mid-afternoon.
A small park on the street of the same name, a block from the sand — shade, benches and a playground at the end of a beach morning.
Shade, showers and parking at the southern end of the beach strip, where the crowd thins out.

landmarks.n: Nhà thờ Đức Mẹ Sao Biển
landmarks.note: Our Lady Star of the Sea, the seaside parish church at the southern end of the beach road.
A statue of Âu Cơ, the legendary mother of the Vietnamese, standing on the seafront at the northern end of the strip.
The small parish church inside the An Thượng grid of hostels and bars, one street back from the seafood row.

routes.name: Beach Strip Morning
routes.blurb: Market first for the price you should be paying, then north up the sand.

stops.tip: Check what seafood costs here before you sit down anywhere on the beach road.
Coffee at the An Thượng end. The bars open late; the cafés open early.
Swim before nine. After that the sand is too hot to cross barefoot.
Showers and shade at the public park end.

art._note: Tranh vẽ tay dùng làm nền. HAI MỐC LÀ ƯỚC LƯỢNG, không phải điểm khảo sát — cả vùng chỉ là một dải bờ gần thẳng, không có vật mốc nào chấm được chắc chắn, và đa giác nước trong dữ liệu chỉ phủ một phần ba phía nam. Hai mốc đặt trên CÙNG một kinh tuyến chạy dọc mép nước (108.2472) nên phép neo không xoay, và căng theo chiều bắc-nam sao cho tranh phủ trọn dải ghim 3,15km. Đã kiểm bằng cách vẽ đè cả 23 ghim: điểm bãi biển rơi trên cát, quán và chợ rơi trong lưới phố. Sai số ngang ước chừng ±100m — đủ chỉ đúng khối phố, không đủ chỉ đúng mặt tiền. Muốn chính xác hơn thì phải bổ sung đường bờ biển phía bắc vào data/maps.json rồi chấm lại.
art.alt: Illustrated aerial map of My Khe beach and the seafront grid in Da Nang

landmarks.note: The walled palace city of the Nguyễn emperors. Enter at Ngọ Môn; allow half a day inside.
The five-phoenix gate on the 50,000₫ note. The centre door was used by exactly one person.
The tallest flagpole in Vietnam, on three stepped terraces facing the river.
Six spans of Eiffel-era steel over the Perfume River, lit in changing colour after dark.
Huế's central market since 1899. The cooked-food row is the cheapest bún bò in town.

landmarks.n: Bảo tàng Cổ vật Cung đình Huế
landmarks.note: Court dress, ceramics and furniture in a wooden palace hall moved here in 1923.
A royal pagoda on the canal, with a painted dragon ceiling uncovered during restoration.
The riverside pavilion where exam results were announced. On the 50,000₫ note beside Ngọ Môn.
The emperor's landing stage on the river, a few steps from Phu Văn Lâu.
The lotus lake inside the citadel walls. In flower from May to August.

landmarks.n: Phố đi bộ Nguyễn Đình Chiểu
landmarks.note: The south-bank river promenade, closed to traffic in the evening.
The moat bridge at Thuong Tu gate, the corner most visitors enter the citadel by after crossing Truong Tien.
The bridge over Da Vien islet at the western end of the riverfront, and the calmest place to watch the Perfume river at dusk.
Crosses the Dong Ba canal into the Gia Hoi quarter — the old merchant district of assembly halls and family temples.
The workhorse road bridge upstream of Truong Tien — most of the city's traffic crosses here, which is why Truong Tien stays walkable.
The vaulted water gate where the Ngu Ha canal leaves the citadel, an easy piece of 19th-century engineering to walk past unnoticed.
The Hue branch, on the river road: the years the family spent in this city, and the school he attended nearby.
The largest of the nine bronze urns cast in the 1830s, standing before the dynastic temple. Their carvings entered UNESCO's memory register in 2024.
The west gate of the Imperial City, the one the court's women used. Far fewer people come in this way than through Ngo Mon.
The market for the wards inside the citadel walls — vegetables, sweets and breakfast stalls, almost no visitors.
Khai Dinh's 1917 palace, European outside and Vietnamese in its painted halls. Bao Dai's family lived here after the abdication.
The queen mother's palace inside the Imperial City, and the most complete wooden complex left standing — verandas, garden and all.
A garden palace in the north-west corner of the Imperial City, built for the dowagers to retire into. Quiet even on busy days.
A long park on the river islet, reached from the bridge — joggers at six, families at six in the evening.
The riverside lawn in front of the flag tower, where the city gathers after dark for kites, coffee carts and skateboards.

routes.name: Citadel Loop
routes.blurb: Breakfast at the market, the palace while it is cool, then out to the river.

stops.tip: Bún bò upstairs, from about six in the morning.
Buy the combined ticket here if you also want the tombs.
Both pavilions on the river bank are free and usually empty.
Cross on foot at dusk, when the bridge lighting starts cycling.

art._note: Tranh vẽ tay dùng làm nền, KHÔNG PHẢI BẮC Ở TRÊN: người vẽ quay cả cảnh 56° cho Kinh thành nằm vuông góc khung. Phép neo hai mốc mang sẵn phần quay đó, nên ghim vẫn đúng chỗ — và vì quay, sông Hương chảy ngang mép dưới tranh lại trùng đúng hướng đông-nam thật của nó. Hai mốc: trung tâm Đại Nội và cầu Trường Tiền.
art.alt: Illustrated aerial map of the Hue citadel and the Perfume river
